properties.title: Tenneco Announces Job Cuts in Spring Hill Plant
properties.summary: Tenneco, Inc. has revealed plans to eliminate 82 jobs at its Spring Hill, Tennessee plant by the end of the year. This decision marks a significant reduction in workforce as the company adjusts its operations.

properties.title: Tenneco Restructuring Affects 200 Jobs in Speyer
properties.summary: Tenneco Inc. has announced that approximately 200 employees in Speyer, Germany, will be impacted by its recent restructuring efforts aimed at cost reduction. This move is part of a broader trend that has seen the company reduce its workforce by about a quarter over the past four years, raising significant concerns about job security among its employees.

properties.title: Massive Strike at Tenneco Inc. Amid Labor Unrest in Belgium
properties.summary: Tenneco Inc. in Sint-Truiden has seen a massive strike, with 90% of its workforce halting production in response to proposed government reforms affecting job security and working conditions. The strike, which involves around 250 employees, is a significant escalation in ongoing labor unrest linked to broader protests across Belgium.

properties.title: Moody's Places Tenneco's Credit Rating Under Review Amid Economic Turbulence
properties.summary: Tenneco Inc. faces ongoing financial pressure as Moody's has placed its credit rating under review for the next 12 months due to rising costs and inflation. The rating agency will evaluate Tenneco's mergers and acquisitions as well as liquidity to determine future ratings, reflecting the company's struggle to maintain margins amid a turbulent economic landscape.

properties.title: Low Acceptance of Tenneco's Voluntary Departure Offer
properties.summary: Only 6 employees have accepted Tenneco's voluntary departure offer, with another 6 nearing completion of the process. Despite 56 expressing interest, enthusiasm is low due to concerns over the reduced financial benefits, as departing employees would receive less than half of the estimated premium of 1,500 to 2,000 euros per year.

properties.title: Tenneco's Layoff Notification Delay Raises Compliance Concerns
properties.summary: Tenneco has announced a significant delay in notifying the Tennessee Department of Labor about upcoming layoffs at its Spring Hill plant, with the notice coming 333 days after the legally required 60-day period. This oversight has sparked concerns regarding compliance with labor regulations, although local officials were informed in a timely manner. The situation underscores ongoing challenges in the automotive sector, which has seen multiple layoffs recently.

properties.title: IGBCE Union Supports Glinde Workers Amid Job Cuts
properties.summary: The IGBCE union, under the leadership of Michael Vassiliadis, has taken a proactive role in supporting Glinde workers during their recent Betriebsversammlung. Vassiliadis emphasized the union's commitment to social agreements, even as the goal of preserving all jobs remains unfulfilled. The article highlights the workforce's strong solidarity and organized protests against the job cuts.

properties.title: Fire Incident at Tenneco Inc. Facility in Belgium
properties.summary: A fire incident occurred at Tenneco Inc.'s manufacturing facility in Sint-Truiden, Belgium, but was swiftly controlled by local fire brigades. Fortunately, all 900 employees were evacuated safely, and no injuries were reported. The cause of the fire remains under investigation as the company collaborates with fire officials.

properties.title: Tenneco Inc. Terminates Collective Agreement, Sparks Layoffs and Union Outcry
properties.summary: Tenneco Inc. has announced the extraordinary termination of the 2022 supplementary collective agreement at its Blumberg plant, effective August 2025. This unexpected decision has resulted in immediate layoffs and has drawn significant criticism from the IG Metall union and the plant's works council chairman, raising alarms about the future of employee rights and benefits.

properties.summary: Environmental groups have escalated their fight against Tenneco's environmental permit by appealing to the Raad voor Vergunningsbetwistingen after their initial appeal was rejected. They are urging for a comprehensive study of the Melsterbeek due to concerning PFAS levels and are challenging the permit's chromium discharge limits, advocating for more rigorous health and environmental evaluations.

properties.summary: Residents near Tenneco's Badalona factory have formally filed complaints to join the ongoing legal case against the company, citing serious health issues linked to emissions. Among the complainants are individuals battling cancer and respiratory illnesses, with some seeking to act as private prosecutors. This legal action is bolstered by new findings of excessive pollution levels and a court-ordered risk analysis to assess the environmental impact of the factory's emissions.

properties.summary: The Badalona City Council has initiated a disciplinary file against Tenneco following alarming findings from a police report that indicates a significant cancer risk linked to the company's emissions. This action comes after a nearly two-year investigation, which revealed elevated levels of toxic metals in the vicinity of the factory and testimonies from workers suffering from serious health issues. Tenneco has responded by asserting its compliance with environmental regulations and disputing the claims made against it.

Tenneco, Inc., was initiated in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan on March 24, 2025, and is identified by case number 2:2025cv10813.

properties.title: Tenneco Confirms Employee Transfers Amid Union Protests
properties.summary: Tenneco has officially confirmed the transfer of 111 employees from its Cuorgnè plant to the Chivasso site, leaving only 29 workers behind. This announcement was made during a meeting with union representatives, who expressed concerns over the future of the Cuorgnè facility and the potential for job losses. In response, unions have organized strikes and are planning further protests to address their grievances.

properties.title: Tenneco Announces Major Job Cuts in Glinde, Sparking Employee Protests
properties.summary: Tenneco has announced a significant workforce reduction at its Glinde facility, planning to cut jobs from 450 to 121 by 2027, which has sparked immediate employee protests and calls for a socially responsible transition. The company also intends to close its brake pad manufacturing plant and relocate production to Romania, further intensifying the backlash from unions and the works council as they prepare for negotiations with management.

properties.title: BRTC Launches Support Program for Displaced Tenneco Workers
properties.summary: Black River Technical College (BRTC) is stepping up to assist around 1,100 displaced Tenneco employees by offering a range of credit and non-credit courses. In addition to educational opportunities, BRTC will provide essential support services including career counseling and job placement assistance to facilitate their transition into new jobs.

properties.title: Supreme Court Upholds Ruling Against Tenneco's Arbitration Clause
properties.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court has declined to review a Sixth Circuit ruling that prevents Tenneco Inc. from enforcing its arbitration clause in an ERISA lawsuit. This decision reinforces the Sixth Circuit's stance that Tenneco's arbitration provision violates the effective vindication doctrine, allowing plan participants to seek broader relief. The ruling aligns with similar decisions from other circuits, marking a significant moment for ERISA participants' rights.

properties.title: Tenneco Announces Revised Layoff Numbers Amid Plant Closures
properties.summary: The Tenneco plant in Paragould, Arkansas, is set to close, with the number of layoffs now confirmed at 687, significantly lower than the previously reported 1,100. This adjustment comes as local officials work to support affected workers through job fairs and workforce development initiatives. The company has also announced layoffs at its East El Paso facility, marking the first major manufacturing job cuts in the area since 2023.

properties.summary: The Principality of Asturias is now formally demanding 241,000 euros from Quantum and DSA for the costs of a second decontamination of the aquifer at the former Tenneco plant in Gijón. Authorities have indicated they are ready to pursue legal action if the owners do not comply with this financial demand, highlighting ongoing environmental concerns.

properties.summary: The recent resolution of the environmental controversy sees Tenneco Inc. agreeing to pay 145,300 euros. This payment comes as part of the total decontamination costs, which reached 391,228.61 euros, as reported by the regional government.

properties.summary: A new study by the Flemish Environment Agency has contradicted Tenneco's assertions regarding pollution levels in the Melsterbeek stream, prompting environmental groups to demand a comprehensive investigation. Ronald Jacobs from Natuurpunt highlighted the presence of heavily polluted soil and the deteriorating condition of fish in the stream, criticizing former Environment Minister Zuhal Demir for minimizing the issue. In response, an information evening is scheduled for January 30 in Sint-Truiden to raise public awareness about the environmental concerns.

properties.title: Fire at Tenneco Inc. Raises Concerns Over Employee Unemployment
properties.summary: A fire at Tenneco Inc. in Garennes-sur-Eure on November 29, 2019, was contained by 36 firefighters, but it has raised concerns about potential technical unemployment for approximately 100 employees. properties.summary: A new report highlights Tenneco Inc. as a significant player in the global hydroform parts market for vehicles. This comprehensive analysis covers market trends and regional developments from 2019 to 2031, indicating Tenneco's potential influence in the industry.

properties.title: Tenneco Automotive Issues Recall for Ford Escape Ball Joints
properties.summary: Tenneco Automotive (DRiV) is recalling 21,664 aftermarket ball joints for 2013-2019 Ford Escape vehicles due to a potential safety issue where the ball joint may separate. Customers will begin receiving notifications about the recall on October 21, 2024, and are encouraged to reach out to DRiV customer service for further details.

properties.title: Tenneco Inc. Reduces Layoffs at Zona Franca Factory
properties.summary: Tenneco Inc. has reached a pre-agreement with union representatives to reduce the number of layoffs at its Zona Franca factory from 70 to 60 employees. This agreement includes a voluntary resignation option with a €2,500 bonus and improved severance terms, which has garnered support from unions such as CGT, CCOO, UGT, and USO. The pre-agreement aims to stabilize employment until 2027, amidst ongoing concerns about the factory's future and health issues related to toxic exposures.

properties.title: Tenneco Inc. Loses Federal Jurisdiction in Legal Dispute with IRG Kettering I LLC
properties.summary: Tenneco Inc. has faced a legal setback as a federal court has remanded its case against IRG Kettering I LLC back to state court. The court determined that Tenneco lacked the necessary diversity jurisdiction due to the complex structure of IRG's ownership, which includes a sub-member LLC trust. This decision effectively ends the federal proceedings and returns the dispute to the Civil Division of the Court of Common Pleas in Montgomery County, Ohio.

properties.title: Tenneco Announces Layoffs at Sint-Truiden Facility
properties.summary: Tenneco has announced layoffs affecting 24 employees at its Sint-Truiden facility, following a special works council meeting. properties.title: Tenneco Meets PFOS Discharge Standards Amid Ongoing Environmental Concerns
